summary.one_liner: bottom (btm) is a customizable, cross-platform graphical process and system monitor for the terminal, supporting Linux, macOS, and Windows.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes a terminal monitor that charts CPU usage (average and per-core), RAM and swap, network I/O, temperature, and disk I/O over time, with zoom in and out of the displayed interval. It also has widgets for disk capacity, temperature sensors, and battery, plus a process widget that supports sorting, searching, kill signals, and tree mode. Behaviour can be set through command-line options or a config file, including colour themes, widget layout, and filtering entries. An htop-inspired basic mode and a single-widget expanded view are also mentioned. A config file is generated on first launch. Installation options span many package managers, and pre-built binaries are provided.
use_cases: monitor CPU, memory, and network usage in the terminal
view and kill processes with a searchable process list
watch disk I/O and temperature sensors over time
check battery and disk capacity from the command line
htop-like system monitoring with custom colour themes
notable: Graphical time-series charts for CPU, memory, network, temperature, and disk I/O in a terminal UI
Tree mode and kill signals in the process widget
Built-in and custom colour themes, with configurable layout via flags or config file
Shell auto-completion files for Bash, Zsh, fish, PowerShell, Elvish, Fig, and Nushell
Packaged for a wide range of Linux, macOS, Windows, and BSD-adjacent package managers
caveats: Officially supports only macOS (x86_64, aarch64), Linux (x86_64, i686, aarch64), and Windows (x86_64, i686); other platforms are unofficial and may not be tested
Some COPR packages are noted as unmaintained and possibly outdated
Building from source requires a recent stable Rust toolchain
keywords: see what is using my cpu
